reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes funding multiple positions in a two-legged binary structure, including positions for family members and a partner, to generate referral and binary bonuses. It presents illustrative weekly returns of 6% to 8% and claims approximately 50% in one year, at least 100% in two years, and that the income will continue for life, then encourages viewers to show the opportunity to friends. These claims and the recruitment-dependent earning structure actively solicit participation rather than merely explaining or criticizing it.

citations.quote: Start with $200 in your own position, then a position in the PowerLeg for a family member perhaps your mother who will not be interested in going online every day and fund this account with $100.
you are binary qualified. Let's now look at earnings in an average week where you earn 7%.

The reality is that within a year you have earned approximately 50% of the value of your smallest leg based on the success of the trading. In 2 years you have received bonuses equivalent to or more than the value of the smaller leg of your business, and it will simply continue.
Now imagine what could happen if you show this to your friends and they started

opening.argument: The presentation frames its figures as conditional illustrations rather than promises. It expressly says the examples are estimates for illustration, and the displayed calculations carry a warning that they are based on history and future results cannot be guaranteed. That qualification matters: hypothetical weekly figures and longer-term projections are presented as scenarios for evaluating a membership model, not as certain outcomes. The Bitcoin discussion is likewise conditional, referring to an added advantage when Bitcoin's value rises. A careful viewer is therefore given uncertainty language alongside the projections, which is inconsistent with treating every displayed percentage as guaranteed income.

citations.quote: Please note that this is a simple estimate for illustration purposes only.
Again please note this is a simple estimate for illustration purposes only.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes the percentages and long-term figures but omits the qualifications attached to the presentation. The seven-percent example is introduced as an average-week scenario, while the slides visibly state that the figures are based on history and future results cannot be guaranteed. The two-year language therefore cannot fairly be read in isolation as a promise of payment; it is part of a projection accompanied by an explicit warning.

citations.quote: Let's now look at earnings in an average week where you earn 7%.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not neutralize the substance of the pitch. The material still presents concrete 6% to 8% weekly scenarios and states that bonuses will continue, while directing the viewer toward a membership structure. Saying future results cannot be guaranteed may qualify the prediction, but it does not turn a promotional earnings presentation into neutral market commentary.

citations.quote: The reality is that within a year you have earned approximately 50% of the value of your smallest leg based on the success of the trading.
Let's now assume that the weekly earning is 6%.

opening.argument: The video's central activity is operational instruction: it explains how to identify the Power Leg and Team Leg, how positions are allocated, and how balances and bonuses are calculated. It even says the viewer can use the system without recruiting anyone. The examples show account placement and arithmetic step by step, including how funds may be moved into a partner's position. That is a tutorial about using a membership system, not evidence that the creator is falsely certifying an outcome. The later invitation to ask questions does not change the instructional format or establish that anyone was actually recruited.

citations.quote: let's look at what you can do to maximise your membership to your full benefit and take advantage of the system without recruiting a single person.
If you see people under you in the 2-legged binary structure, are they going to the left or to the right?
You could draw the extra one hundred and fourteen dollars twenty four and go shopping or you could simply withdraw that and add it to your partner's position in your team leg
If you have questions, or for more information, please contact Clint.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not answer what it teaches. The instructions are specifically about funding positions in two legs, becoming binary qualified, and increasing bonuses through the smaller leg. The fact that recruitment is initially described as unnecessary does not erase the later discussion of friends joining the team leg. The video's instructional form is therefore compatible with, rather than separate from, a solicitation.

citations.quote: Start with $200 in your own position, then a position in the PowerLeg for a family member
you are binary qualified.
Now imagine what could happen if you show this to your friends and they started

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanics being explained do not make the presentation a scam. Educational content can describe how a service operates, including its account structure and bonus calculations. The opening's phrase about acting without recruitment directly undermines the claim that recruitment is necessary to participate, and the evidence does not show that any viewer joined or that any promised result occurred.

citations.quote: take advantage of the system without recruiting a single person.
Please note that this is a simple estimate for illustration purposes only.

opening.argument: The evidence supports a membership and trading service being explained and promoted, but it does not establish the mechanisms that would independently make it fraudulent. The material does not show a request for passwords, identity documents, or other credentials, and it does not document a completed payment, a concealed fee, or a failed withdrawal. It describes positions, balances, and bonuses, while identifying the currency as Bitcoin or BITS. Referral and binary bonuses may be features of the service's compensation plan, but the supplied material does not prove that participant funds come solely from new recruits or that the underlying trading activity is fictitious. Promotion alone is not proof of a scam.

citations.quote: all currency on the Mirror Trading International platform is stated in Bitcoin or BITS
The trading bonuses for your 3 positions is thus $64.20
Please note that binary bonuses and referral bonuses are paid into your activation wallet a week in arrears.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The issue is not whether the video requests passwords or documents. It actively explains how to fund three positions, obtain referral and binary bonuses, and enlarge the smaller leg. It also connects the opportunity to friends joining the team leg. Those are not merely ordinary retail-service details; they describe the earning mechanism presented to participants. The absence of a credential request does not answer whether the compensation structure is recruitment-dependent.

citations.quote: Then open a position for your partner in your TeamLeg.
you receive the full benefit from the binary in your smaller leg.
Now imagine what could happen if you show this to your friends and they started

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited mechanics still do not establish that the service lacks genuine trading or that returns are funded by recruitment. The material calls the amounts trading bonuses, identifies an activation wallet, and repeatedly qualifies the numerical examples as estimates. A binary compensation feature and an invitation to tell friends may be promotional, but the supplied evidence does not prove fraud rather than an ordinary membership referral arrangement.
